messages:
Maria (CS): forwarding an urgent escalation from a customer — they started seeing translation / non-English quality regressions after last rollout (redwood-3.2.1). customer says spanish and vietnamese outputs are frequently wrong or in English. examples below, original reported at 2026-02-18T22:14Z.

Maria (CS): Customer quote: "When I ask in Spanish the model sometimes replies in English or strips diacritics. Example prompt: 'Traduce al español: ¿Dónde está la estación?' -> Response: 'Where is the station' (English). Also Vietnamese diacritics are mangled. This started after the update." :flag_es: :flag_vn:

Liang (Support): thanks — can you paste the exact API payloads + model + region + response ids?

Maria (CS): pasted by customer:
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Body: {"model":"redwood-3.2.1","input":"Traduce al español: ¿Dónde está la estación?","region":"eu-west-1","max_tokens":60}
Response id: req_0a1b2c3d
```

Liang (Support): have they tried pinning to previous model? are both APAC and EU affected?

Maria (CS): customer says 3.1.9 returns correct Spanish with diacritics. issue reproduced in APAC and EU for them.

Runtime Bot: Deploy job #deploy-2313 completed at 2026-02-18T22:12:23Z. variant 'redwood-3.2.1-quant' routed: EU 60%, APAC 100%.

Olivia (Eng): @Liang @SRE Oncall noted: rollout included two changes simultaneously — a tokenizer normalization patch (utf8-normalize) and a new quantization profile to reduce memory. I suspect interaction between tokenizer folding and quantization on short-context translations.

Liang (Support): can you repro locally with the exact request id? Maria can you ask customer to run a small repro set and return response ids?

Maria (CS): asked customer to run these three prompts and paste response ids: 
1) "Traduce al español: ¿Dónde está la estación?"
2) "Dịch sang tiếng Việt: Tôi cần tìm nhà ga gần nhất"
3) "日本語で：お名前は何ですか？"
Provided curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-3.2.1","input":"Traduce al español: ¿Dónde está la estación?","max_tokens":40}'
```

Maria (CS): customer returned ids: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0d4e5f6g, req_0h9i0j1k and notes 3.1.9 returns correct accented/diacritic-preserving text.

Olivia (Eng): reproed locally — observed that 3.2.1 with the quant profile sometimes maps accented unicode sequences to ASCII-equivalents in short prompts when an eviction from KV cache occurs. Tokenizer log excerpt:
```
TOKENIZER DEBUG: input_bytes=34 normalized_bytes=28 fold_map=0x11 OOV_pct=4.2%
KV_CACHE: evict_count=2 last_evicted_key=0x7f3
```
This explains diacritics dropping and odd language fallback for tiny inputs.

Liang (Support): any error logs or latency spikes?

Olivia (Eng): no exceptions, just tokenization mapping anomalies combined with quantized weight rounding. Looks like the utf8-normalize change changed byte-level normalization order so the quant kernels saw slightly different token ids for some unicode sequences.

SRE Oncall: can we mitigate quickly? APAC seems worst-hit because it was routed 100% to the new variant.

Olivia (Eng): mitigation plan: 1) pin APAC traffic to 3.1.9 for translation-sensitive customers, 2) rollback quant profile in EU while we hotfix tokenizer + add regression tests. Patch ETA ~6h.

Runtime Bot: Route change requested by SRE Oncall (action id: route-789).

SRE Oncall: applied route change — APAC now pinned to redwood-3.1.9 as of 2026-02-18T23:05:10Z.

Liang (Support): I'll add a temporary alert for non-English-quality-drop metric and watch the customer cohort. Also flagged dashboards for spanish, vietnamese, japanese short-prompt populations.

Olivia (Eng): working on hotfix: revert utf8-normalize ordering + add tokenization unit tests across 40 languages and short-context flows. root cause summary: interaction of tokenizer normalization + quantized weight rounding produced different token ids for extended unicode sequences in the hot path (continuous batching + kvcache eviction).

Maria (CS): informed customer of rollback and mitigation steps, asked for confirmation and any additional failing examples. Customer responded: "thanks for the fast response — waiting to confirm once APAC rollback completes" :pray:

SRE Oncall: metrics update — spanish-regression-alert decreased 85% in APAC after pinning, overall translation complaints down.

Maria (CS): closing this thread as provisional. will re-open if customer sees any residual regression after the hotfix. thanks everyone.
